questions.worked_solution:
Using the linearity property of double integrals, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{R}\frac{1-3x{y}^{2}}{x}\,\text{d}A & ={∬}_{R}(\frac{1}{x}-3{y}^{2})\,\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{R}\frac{1}{x}\,\text{d}A-{∬}_{R}3{y}^{2}\text{ }\text{d}A.\end{aligned}
$$

The function under the first integral is independent of $y.$ So, we have 

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{R}\frac{1}{x}\text{ }\text{d}A & =(3-2){\int }_{1}^{e}\frac{1}{x}\,\text{d}x \\  & =[\operatorname{ln}⁡|x|]_{1}^{e} \\  & =\operatorname{ln}⁡(e)-\operatorname{ln}⁡(1) \\  & =1.\end{aligned}
$$

The function under the second integral is independent of $x.$ So, we have 

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{R}3{y}^{2}\text{ }\text{d}A & =(e-1){\int }_{2}^{3}3{y}^{2}\,\text{d}y \\  & =(e-1)[{y}^{3}]_{2}^{3} \\  & =(e-1)({3}^{3}-{2}^{3}) \\  & =19(e-1).\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, combining our results, we obtain 

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{R}\frac{1-3x{y}^{2}}{x}\,\text{d}A=1-19(e-1)=20-19e.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.worked_solution:
First, notice that the domain $R$ can be represented as a union of three sub-domains, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}R & =S\cup T\cup U.\end{aligned}

So, we can write

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{R}f(x,y)\,\text{d}A & ={∬}_{S}f(x,y)\,\text{d}A+{∬}_{T}f(x,y)\,\text{d}A+{∬}_{U}f(x,y)\,\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{S}x\,\text{d}A+{∬}_{T}0\,\text{d}A+{∬}_{U}{x}^{2}y\,\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{S}x\,\text{d}A+{∬}_{U}{x}^{2}y\,\text{d}A.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem:
Given that $C$ and $D$ are finite, non-overlapping regions and that

$$
{∬}_{C}f(x,y)\text{ }\text{d}A=-3,\,{∬}_{D}f(x,y)\text{ }\text{d}A=5,
$$

find the value of 

$$
{∬}_{C\cup D}-2f(x,y)\text{ }\text{d}A.
$$
questions.worked_solution:
Using the linearity and additivity of double integrals, we get the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{C\cup D}-2f(x,y)\text{ }\text{d}A & =-2\cdot \,\,\,{∬}_{C\cup D}f(x,y)\text{ }\text{d}A \\  & =-2\cdot ({∬}_{C}f(x,y)\text{ }\text{d}A+{∬}_{D}f(x,y)\text{ }\text{d}A) \\  & =-2\cdot (-3+5) \\  & =-4\end{aligned}
$$
